superseded.why: v0.5.1: the daily limit kept spend in 24 hourly buckets, so a full limit spent late in an hour stopped counting 23h01m later and twice the limit could go out within 24 hours (superseded by 0.5.2, which counts a bucket for 25 hours)

v0.5.0: an invoice paid at a vendor's EVM sub-account before its link was recorded could be paid again at the main account; a sub-account link could be re-pointed; a held payment whose signatures stood again after a co-approver's ME ID lapsed and came back could not be released (superseded by 0.5.1)

v0.4: an invoice paid at a vendor's main account could be paid again at its registered EVM sub-account, and an owner's (or co-approver's) own sub-account counted as a second person for two-person approval (superseded by 0.5)
v0.3: an agent key that also held an ME ID could pay itself through its registered EVM sub-account; no co-approvers (superseded by 0.4)
v0.2: no EVM sub-account resolution, no fixed-deposit bond, no identity query (superseded by 0.3, same accounting rules)

v0.1: a revoke could be lifted by update_policy, invoice numbers matched byte-for-byte ("inv 1001" paid INV-1001 again), the daily limit reset at UTC midnight, anyone could register an agent address they did not control, and it had a migrate admin. All fixed in 0.2 (CHANGELOG.md).
approve did not re-check the owner's ME ID (a suspended owner could still release held payments); duplicate invoices were reported after limit errors; built on macOS, not the canonical Linux build
emitted an empty vendor_did attribute, which wasmd rejects, so every payment to a vendor without an ME ID failed
